events.title: Hot Seat: every player gets their own controller
events.summary: Playing Hot Seat with more than one controller? Now each controller belongs to its player and works only on that player's turn. No more friendly "help" on someone else's turn :)How it works:- The first time you start a match with two or more controllers, press any button on a controller. A window opens: pick your name with the d-pad and press A. Then the same with the other controller.- The controller number shows next to each player's name.- Press X any time to open the window again and change

events.title: Now on macOS
events.summary: The full version for macOS users, with cross-play against Windows. Android and iOS are already in closed testing — we are getting ready to let you play with them too.The same patch brings a set of tips to both versions, Windows and macOS, based on feedback from players who sat down to the game for the first time. They make a newcomer’s first hour easier.There is a pinned thread on the community page for your wishes.

events.title: The demo is now fully playable with a gamepad
events.summary: As someone whose computer has replaced almost all other devices for the last 30 years, I had no idea how many people play with game controllers.But when I started looking into how important this kind of support is for others, I realized that for many people a mouse is not always the best choice.So I spent the last week adding game controller support to my game as well.I'll be glad if it's more comfortable for you now.For any problems, write in the Community Hub or email support@dam-n.com

events.title: Card canceling feature
events.summary: Cancel a card selection by clicking the card again or pressing Esc.

events.title: Critical fix for online functionality
events.summary: Two critical online issues have been fixed in the Demo: The online login now renews itself, so the session no longer drops after an hour of continuous play. The game no longer freezes when you quickly double-click a piece or a card during your turn. We also made several changes players asked for: Removed the automatic dimming of all pieces except yours at the start of a turn. Instead, a button at the bottom of the screen turns this view on and off. You can do the same with the right mouse button

events.title: The D.A.M.N! demo is out
events.summary: I am glad to say that from today you can try, for free, what my family has been making. They worked on making the game interesting and competitive, and friends of mine who are artists made it look and sound fun. Some of you will recognise the classic cross-shaped board, the same one as in Ludo or Mensch ärgere Dich nicht.
